the use of conductive pastes, or the brazing, allows to obtain a great reduction of thermal resistance, and, consequently, an increase of the heat transfer coefficients, with respect to the simple contact.
the use of a thermal paste and a proper brazing contact is highly recommended for the application of metal foams in forced convection.

the thermal contact resistance is the main parameter to be considered when designing a forced convection heat transfer system with metal foams, and its influence is more evident for the case of the simple contact between the sample and base plate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in forced convection, the thermal contact resistance is the main limiting factor for heat transfer enhancement, especially in the case of simple contacts.
the thermal contact resistance of aluminum foam in forced convection has a significant effect on the overall thermal resistance.
, for a given heat transfer rate, the use of a paste or a brazing contact allows to reduce the size of the cooling system, compared with the case of a simple contact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a fixed value of the thermal conductivity and of the porosity, it is possible to increase the heat transfer performance of the metal foam, simply by reducing the contact resistance.

the thermal contact resistance can play a significant role in determining the overall thermal resistance, and therefore the heat transfer coefficient, especially when the thermal contact resistance is not negligible.

the use of conductive paste and brazing is recommended in the design of heat exchangers based on the use of metal foams, as they allow to significantly reduce the global thermal resistance and to increase the global heat transfer coefficients.
